status: Actual core wire spellings plus still-proposed provider spellings; documentation only, never a runtime implementation registry.

donor.retention: provider-api-evidence.json retains source bindings; git show REV:path reproduces donor sources

rules.ids: Stable first-party action names; schema versions occupy their existing independent core fields. External providers choose their own unique IDs.
rules.codecVersion: Each selected provider-local intent, receipt, observation and present native-error codec starts at the exact string 1. The pair of definitionId and channel selects the codec; there is no version discovery or fallback.
rules.payloads: Native source symbols identify provider-private payload facts/refinements to retain, not wholesale adoption of legacy framework envelopes or reconciliation classes. This projection introduces no new payload fields or public codec exports.
rules.failure: Known native response-decoding errors use dispatchError version 1 and remain Inconclusive. Other transport failures retain core-dispatch-error/1. No first-party rejection proof codec is selected; absent or malformed provider data and non-success HTTP status do not authorize replay.
rules.scope: RequestFacts.scope is the exact kernel-canonical JSON encoding of the strict two-field object {definitionId,coordinate}. coordinate has exactly the keys in the operation row, with string values derived from the decoded intent; no extra properties. Principal stays in RequestFacts.principal. No secrets or URLs containing secrets.
rules.normalization: Validate native coordinate syntax and require its canonical form before authoring; reject aliases rather than silently normalizing frozen inputs. Scope construction never changes external request-body serialization.
rules.versionPolicy: A changed encoded native meaning requires a new local channel version; one selected implementation admits one exact version. No legacy reader is implied.
rules.evidence: Literal and coordinate choices are proposed integration details. Frozen research IDs, scope strings, payload bytes and digests remain unchanged and are not claimed to have tested these target spellings.

coordinate.kind: AppPreparation -> app; DmgPreparation -> dmg; PkgPreparation -> pkg

associations.github: Parent operation IDs remain immutable coordinates. Native annotated-object OID, releaseId and uploadUrlTemplate are resolved only from matching admitted parent receipt/observation; endpoint/body/native evidence correspondence binds the resolved IDs. Scope does not acquire a second spelling after parent resolution.
associations.git: CommitInput.scope and Intent.scope must already equal canonical {definitionId:ts-release/git.update-ref,coordinate:{remote,ref}}. Selected catalogs combine all managed file edits for one authority/remote/ref into one commit operation; reject duplicate operations for that authority/coordinate. The captured native closure additionally verifies old/new OIDs, objectSet Content and exact argv.
associations.apple: One definition decodes the full three-kind ApplePreparation union. App dispatch calls Notary.submitApp; DMG/pkg dispatch calls Notary.submit. Scope credentialRef is a public credential selector; native Client is host-owned. Receipt stays Pending until matching native observation and one CAS-selected ReadyToPlan. No separate staple, assessment or Ready publication definition exists.
associations.stores: JournalStore scope/auth configuration belongs to the backend and is not a provider operation. The remote journal ref/CAS and global journalId laws remain host-api/journal-store contracts; this operation-scope projection creates no store definitionId.

result.reason: A nonsecret diagnostic string describing the native failure

nativeDispatchErrorMapping.rule: The selected provider decoder or Apple opaque transport returns this value through Effect success. It must not fail the transport Effect with the native error. The kernel admits the payload using the owning dispatchError codec and corresponds(operation,request,evidence), then appends ObservationRecorded with evidenceKind DispatchError, status Inconclusive, and evidenceVersion 1.
nativeDispatchErrorMapping.coreFailureContrast: Effect failure typed ReleaseError is caught by the kernel and persists only its code/message as core-dispatch-error/1. It does not preserve an attached native error payload.
nativeDispatchErrorMapping.http: Each HttpProviderDefinition.decodeResponse maps its listed known native response-decoding error to Unknown with encoded nativeError. Root makeHttpTransport returns that SendResult unchanged. Native reason/status/commitment fields remain evidence and never select replay or Satisfied by themselves.
nativeDispatchErrorMapping.apple: Only actual Notary.SubmissionOutcomeUnknown is selected for the Apple provider's durable native dispatch-error codec. The opaque transport catches that specific tagged failure and returns Unknown with its exact encoded public payload. Other NativeAppleError members remain typed function failures; this contract does not claim they are all journaled losslessly.

nativeDispatchErrorMapping.coverage: Kernel native-error persistence and the frozen app SubmissionOutcomeUnknown path have local protocol evidence. Full provider decoder adaptations to these proposed IDs/versions remain implementation work. No hosted response/native Apple acceptance is claimed.

appleOpaqueRequest.body: UTF8(kernel canonical(Schema.encodeSync(ApplePreparation)(input))) using the complete admitted AppPreparation | DmgPreparation | PkgPreparation union member
appleOpaqueRequest.scope: The exact canonical definitionId/coordinate value specified by the Apple.preparationProvider row; kind is app, dmg or pkg according to the input tag
appleOpaqueRequest.construction: Use kernel makeRequest once to derive bodyDigest and canonical decimal byteLength. The body binds the native input, owned source, signature, journal root, public credential selector and producer revision. It is an opaque invocation descriptor, not the native ZIP or notarytool wire payload.
appleOpaqueRequest.dispatch: The captured transport strictly decodes the body as ApplePreparation, re-derives all request facts and verifies their correspondence before restoring owned bytes or obtaining the native client. App calls Notary.submitApp({bundle}); DMG/pkg call Notary.submit({kind,artifact}) with their exact restored public native type.

hashCanonical.algorithm: SHA-256 over UTF8(decimal byte length of domain + ':' + domain + decimal byte length of canonical payload + ':' + canonical payload); no NUL separators

operation.preimage: {definitionId,intentVersion,intent}; operation dependsOn is not part of operationId

plan.preimage: {format,bundleId,operations sorted by operationId,journalId}; each operation retains sorted dependsOn

defaultJournal.preimage: {format:ts-release/plan/1,bundleId,operations sorted by operationId}; used only without explicit collection-bound journalId

request.preimage: complete RequestFacts, including nonsecret headers, bodyDigest, decimal byteLength, principal, scope and replay

appleCollection.preimage: caller-ordered encoded ApplePreparation members with every derived member journalId omitted

rawHashes: Content.sha256 is SHA-256 of exact owned bytes; decimal Content.bytes is their byte count.
Plan.bundleId is final bundle Content.sha256. Bundle bytes are exact UTF8(JSON.stringify(Schema.encode(Bundle))); artifact order is caller identity, not a new sorted inventory.

Upstream file/executable identity is native digest over bytes. Upstream tree digest is SHA-256 of its exact ordered JSON.stringify({rootMode,totalBytes,entries}) manifest; never re-encode it with kernel canonical JSON.
Git SHA-1/SHA-256 OIDs use Git native object hashing, independently of owned Content SHA-256. Owned core-git-object-set/v1 bytes have their own Content hash.
transientOnly: preparation:<operationId> bundleId on reconstructed preparation Plan view
rootVocabulary.noAdditionalIdentity: No provider request hash, provider plan hash, side journal, replay authority scalar, or checksum peer manifest.

preservedExternalStandards.rule: Keep native package, transport and metadata schemas; local codec versions do not rename native $schema.
Keep exact signed bytes, payload types, issuer/audience and subject digests; local envelope versions cannot rewrite them.
Native registry checksums remain separate from Content SHA-256; no invented upload or publication ID.
Retain selected x-github-api-version and lossless native IDs, tag OIDs and upload URL templates. This is the retained API pin, not a claim it is the newest remote version.
Keep native submission UUID, kind, source identity, opaque ZIP diagnostic digest and actual native tool observations. Local channel version does not alter upstream payload schema.
Keep selected donor wire versions, filename/project rules and exact remote digest facts; compatibility endpoint laws are not inherited from PyPI.
Native object/tree/ref and porcelain laws remain unchanged. core-git-object-set/v1 is a retained local transport container, not a Git-standard format.
